idea.description: Test uniform multi-negative masked-target cross-entropy in the supplied corrected BERT4Rec, with a count-matched baseline-objective control. Train exactly one independent model per category in each configuration. Preserve baseline terminal-mask allocation and reconstruction corruption. Audit the baseline objective and negative count before defining comparisons; use K=16 as the declared multi-negative setting. Retain the unchanged supplied baseline as the benchmark anchor. Comparison models are separate experiments and are never combined at inference.
idea.motivation: Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have training-exposed negative-beats-positive rates of 12.03% and 10.25%, with negative tenth-percentile margins. More competing items per hidden target may improve contextual discrimination, while candidate cross-entropy changes how those competitors interact during optimization. The proposal explicitly targets two user-facing failures: broadly related adjacent products displacing specifically supported matches, and movie recommendations with weak identifiable connections to history. These links are hypotheses, not measured remedies: uniform negatives may be easy, interaction supervision cannot establish ownership, compatibility, redundancy or current intent, and training errors do not establish held-out quality. Earlier terminal-allocation proposals had lower reported scores than the supplied baseline, motivating an orthogonal experiment without interpreting those historical comparisons as controlled causal evidence. At 10% research progress, strengthen this feasible experiment rather than switching immediately to a more complex text or temporal architecture.
idea.implementation_notes:
Apply the intervention to the supplied corrected baseline; its source is not included here, so this is an implementation specification rather than an executable train.py replacement. Preserve the BERT4Rec architecture, original sampled-window rules, eligible-user distribution, reserved-mask corruption, terminal allocation, optimizer, schedule, clipping and checkpoint-selection policy. Document the actual baseline objective, negative count, proposal, replacement policy, eligibility rules, loss reduction and handling of degenerate examples before configuring comparisons. Do not assume the corrected baseline necessarily uses BCE with one negative.

Comparison design: retain the unchanged supplied baseline as the benchmark anchor. If it uses BCE/K=1, the minimum mechanistic comparison contains a matched BCE/K=1 control, BCE/K=16, and CE/K=16. BCE/K=16 versus BCE/K=1 estimates the negative-count intervention under the declared BCE weighting; CE/K=16 versus BCE/K=16 estimates the objective intervention at matched count. CE/K=16 versus the original baseline estimates the complete practical policy change. A full 2×2 additionally includes CE/K=1, but defer that optional configuration unless budget remains after the minimum complete four-category comparison. If the baseline uses another objective or negative count, substitute its actual objective/count and document which effects are identifiable. If the baseline already matches a planned configuration, avoid redundant training. If budget permits only a baseline-versus-CE comparison, label it explicitly as a combined intervention and do not claim a separated loss effect. Each configuration trains one independent model per category; comparison checkpoints must never be fused, averaged or reused as another trial's initialization.

Randomness isolation: preprocessing remains seed 0 and training remains seed 42. A fixed global seed alone does not preserve sampled examples when K changes. Use purpose-separated generators initialized reproducibly from seed 42 for user/window sampling, masking/replacement, training negatives and loader ordering, or sample-specific seeds composed from stable integers such as (42, category_index, epoch, step, example_index, purpose_id). Use a fixed declared category ordering rather than Python's randomized hash. Keep K out of user/window and corruption seeds. Pass generators explicitly to NumPy and PyTorch operations; seed Python, NumPy and custom generators in loader workers if they are used. Seed model initialization and dropout consistently across matched variants. Introducing isolated streams changes a baseline that previously shared one stream, so use the same stream scheme in every mechanistic comparison and distinguish the resulting matched baseline from the unchanged host baseline. Never attribute that change to CE alone. Verify the matched-example claim using sampled user IDs, original windows, targets, mask positions and corrupted inputs at corresponding steps; record hashes and investigate discrepancies. Matching examples does not imply identical optimization trajectories or cross-platform numerical reproducibility.

Negative sampling: the original proposal used 16 independent uniform draws with replacement. Retain that policy only if compatible with the baseline comparison design; otherwise preserve the baseline replacement policy in both matched objectives and explicitly document the amendment. The priority is identical candidate multisets for CE/K=16 and baseline-objective/K=16. Sample uniformly from each target's eligible training catalog, excluding its positive, PAD and MASK and preserving the baseline's existing observed-history exclusions. Do not silently add full-history exclusions or change the user distribution. Document the eligible-set definition and proposal q. With replacement, repeated negatives retain multiplicity; report duplicate and unique-count statistics. Without replacement, require enough eligible items and predeclare the shared fallback for smaller catalogs. If no eligible negative exists, retain the documented baseline handling, count occurrences and avoid empty or NaN reductions. Use training histories only for exclusion rules; never consult validation or test interactions. Unobserved eligible items remain uncertain negatives rather than verified dislikes.

Define candidate CE explicitly for positive logit p and sampled negative logits n_j: L_CE = log(1 + sum_j exp(n_j-p)), implemented with stable cross-entropy or logsumexp. Use no logQ adjustment. This is a candidate-ranking surrogate, not an unbiased full-catalog likelihood estimator and not an implementation of Correcting the LogQ Correction. At K=1 it equals softplus(n-p), the BPR logistic loss. Its gradients couple candidates through the softmax and it is invariant to a common score shift. BCE instead uses independently anchored logits: its unreduced positive term is softplus(-p), with negative terms softplus(n_j). These distinctions explain why CE and BCE differ even with identical candidates; they do not establish superiority.

Document both within-target and across-target reduction. For a baseline that sums its positive term and averages negative terms, extend it as softplus(-p) + mean_j softplus(n_j). For a baseline that sums every term, retain the corresponding sum and disclose that increasing K also changes gradient scale and positive/negative weighting. For another baseline reduction, write its exact formula and extension before observing results. Preserve baseline weighting across valid target positions and examples. CE has one loss per valid target; apply that same across-target/example weighting, while acknowledging that objective geometry and gradient magnitudes remain different. A repeated negative appearing m times contributes m*exp(n) to CE's denominator, equivalent to n+log(m), and m repeated terms to summed BCE. Do not deduplicate only one objective or introduce post-hoc gradient rescaling. Record target counts, denominator values and branch losses; optional sparse gradient-norm logging must fit the budget.

Do not add hard mining, temporal biases, text features, new terminal allocation, new masking rules or auxiliary fitted scores to the primary experiment. R2NS supports gradual hardness as a future hypothesis; it does not prove that hard candidates are true negatives. The title-residual alternative could address identifiable movie connections more directly, but its scratch-trained encoder, joint optimization and target-text masking create additional work. Temporal attention remains a separate follow-up because the supplied sensitivity results establish no preferred recency direction. These alternatives remain single jointly trained BERT4Rec networks if explored.

Use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42; retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl and their supplied splits. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Respect the host's SASREC_EPOCHS=200 environment default despite its name. All training, diagnostics, debugging and failures count against 43,200 GPU-seconds; four concurrent slots do not reduce summed GPU cost. Prioritize complete four-category comparisons, account for actual runtime and do not launch optional controls without sufficient remaining budget. Never inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints. Supplied historical scores are contextual evidence only.

Prediction loads exactly one selected trained model/checkpoint for the requested category. Retain the final L-1 observed history events, append the reserved MASK, left-pad, and read the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Require the baseline-supported sequence capacity for appended-mask inference. Hide each supervised target at its selected input position during bidirectional training; legitimate earlier occurrences of the same item remain valid historical context. Do not use shifted targets in visible bidirectional inputs. Preserve the embedded predictor writer, architecture configuration, reserved IDs, item mappings and all four routes, even though this experiment changes only training. Exclude PAD and MASK from recommendations. Measure fresh-process checkpoint/predictor score parity before claiming it; live-model identity checks are insufficient.

Preserve family-specific sample_batch and ModelView, including view.model as the actual trained nn.Module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), constructing its prompt from measured metrics and definitions. Diagnostic loader tuples remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L; training-only multi-negative tensors remain internal to the loss. Preserve the original fixed one-negative diagnostic protocol and its reduction-independent positive-minus-negative logit definitions for comparability. Use a disposable diagnostic loader and independent diagnostic RNG rather than consuming the training iterator. Record provenance outside the unchanged loader tuple where supported. Missing sampler provenance, fresh-process parity and attention deletion remain unavailable until actually implemented and measured. Do not interpret reserved-mask validity as proof of provenance. Embedding alignment near 0.5 does not establish collapse, recommendation diversity or representation quality. Omitted history-sensitivity results establish no directional recency conclusion.

Interpret diagnostic margin changes cautiously across objectives. CE does not anchor absolute logits, and neither objective fixes a universal logit scale. A larger raw margin or fewer margins below 0.5 can reflect score scaling as well as changed separation. Preserve the original metrics and additionally emphasize the fixed-candidate negative-beats-positive rate, which is invariant to a common positive score rescaling. Training-exposed diagnostics remain distinct from held-out performance; do not rank trials by their training margins or fabricate unsupported category-metadata breakdowns.

Predeclare comparisons, loss formulas, replacement/fallback rules, stream composition and the unchanged host-compatible validation schedule, checkpoint selection, stopping and tie rules before observing treatment results. Select only using the pinned sampled four-category macro validation HR@10: 200 users/category, one positive plus 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42. Report category hits/200, HR@10, category differences and equally weighted macro differences only from supplied host results. One hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Preserve identical host users and candidates across configurations; do not modify the evaluator or add metric corrections. Training samples need not mimic the evaluator's 99 unique negatives exactly; document the distinction rather than presenting K=16 as an evaluation match.

If the host supplies paired user-level hits, compute 10,000 seed-42 bootstrap resamples of 200 paired users within each category and recompute macro differences; report percentile 95% intervals. Otherwise mark paired uncertainty unavailable. These intervals condition on fixed candidates and fitted models, exclude candidate-sampling bias, training-seed variability and adaptive selection, and do not change deterministic differences on the finite benchmark. Sampled ranking can order models differently from full-catalog ranking. Therefore describe any improvement as a sampled-validation gain, not evidence of better full-catalog HR@10 or actual user usefulness. The twenty-user full-catalog simulator exercise can supply limited qualitative feedback only when genuinely run; it is not a substitute selection metric or proof of broad user benefit.

Main risks are memorizing repeated training targets, fitting frequent or easy negative distinctions, amplifying false-negative errors, selecting favorable validation noise, and mistaking loss-scale changes for improved discrimination. Preserve the baseline regularization and stopping policy, avoid post-hoc tuning of K or reduction, disclose every inspected configuration/checkpoint and all budget use, and freeze final selection before untouched held-out evaluation. No test labels or test metrics enter search. Available data comprise public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable ratings, review text, item categories/prices/stores and simulator diversity/conformity traits must not enter training, diagnostics or explanations. No extra datasets or pretrained weights are needed.

Preserve supplied preprocessing(seed=0), splits, category routing and evaluator.
Audit baseline objective, K0, eligibility, replacement, reductions and selection rules.
Retain unchanged baseline as the practical benchmark anchor.
Declare K=16, controls, loss formulas, RNG scheme and budget allocation.

If baseline is BCE/K=1:
    Required matched configurations = BCE/K=1, BCE/K=16, CE/K=16.
    Optional budgeted configuration = CE/K=1.
Else:
    Adapt controls to actual baseline objective/count; state identifiable effects.
Do not train duplicate configurations when already equivalent.

For each declared configuration:
    For each of the four categories in fixed order:
        Initialize one corrected BERT4Rec with training seed 42.
        Initialize identical purpose-separated RNG schemes across matched controls.
        For epoch in range(at_most_200):
            For step in range(200):
                Sample users/windows with baseline rules and keyed window RNG.
                Construct baseline masked inputs using separate corruption RNG.
                Record example identity/provenance hashes.
                features = model.log2feats(sequence)[valid_target_positions]
                For each positive target y:
                    eligible = documented_baseline_eligible_training_catalog(y)
                    candidates = sample_with_declared_policy(
                        eligible, K_for_configuration,
                        keyed_negative_rng(category, epoch, step, example, target))
                    Apply predeclared empty/small-set fallback if required.
                    logits = model.predict_score(features_y, [y] + candidates)
                    If CE:
                        target_loss = stable_cross_entropy(logits, class_index=0)
                    Else:
                        target_loss = declared_baseline_objective_and_K_reduction(logits)
                loss = unchanged_across_target_and_example_reduction(target_losses)
                Apply unchanged optimizer, schedule and clipping.
                Record counts, denominator, candidate multiplicities and loss.
            Apply unchanged host-compatible validation/checkpoint procedure.
        Save one selected checkpoint with matching configuration and mappings.
    Keep configuration predictions separate; never fuse models.

Verify matching users, windows, targets, masks and corrupted inputs across controls.
Verify identical K=16 candidate multisets for count-matched objective comparisons.
Distinguish unchanged host baseline from any RNG-isolated matched baseline.
Emit matching working/predict.py with all four category routes.

For inference:
    Load exactly one selected checkpoint for the requested category.
    sequence = left_pad(last_L_minus_1(history) + [MASK], L)
    position = greatest_index_where(sequence != PAD)
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)[position]
    return model.predict_score(features, real_candidate_items)
Verify fresh-process predictor/checkpoint parity before claiming it.

Run preserved diagnostic APIs with an independent disposable one-negative loader.
Return measured metrics and definitions; keep unavailable checks explicitly unavailable.
Interpret margins with score-scale caveats; distinguish training diagnostics from validation.
Obtain category hits and macro validation HR@10 only from the pinned host evaluator.
If paired user hits exist, compute 10,000 seed-42 stratified paired bootstrap resamples.
Report uncertainty conditional on fitted models/fixed candidates and its limitations.
Record all trials, checkpoint evaluations, failures and summed GPU-seconds.
Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10 and freeze before held-out evaluation.
Never combine independently trained predictions or average checkpoints.

originality.positive: A diagnosis-driven, count-controlled BERT4Rec comparison can provide useful experimental evidence while preserving masking and inference integrity.
originality.negative: Multi-negative candidate cross-entropy, its K=1 BPR equivalence and count-matched controls are established techniques. Better experimental control strengthens evidence rather than algorithmic novelty.

future_potential.positive: An interpretable result can guide objective selection, controlled sampling research and later jointly trained text or temporal extensions within the same backbone.
future_potential.negative: Uniform negatives may be easy or uncertain, and sampled-validation gains may not improve full-catalog usefulness. The method addresses the reported user failures indirectly and has no demonstrated gain yet.

code_difficulty.positive: The core changes remain localized to negative sampling and training loss; architecture, category routing and appended-mask inference remain unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible RNG isolation, baseline-reduction auditing, matched-candidate controls, provenance verification, diagnostic interpretation and multiple complete comparisons add integration work and GPU cost beyond a simple loss replacement.

idea_diagnosis.description: Instrument the actual corrected BERT4Rec production path with bounded event-level provenance, capture exact consumed batches immediately before model use, and independently replay their construction and loss against supplied training histories. Calibrate assertions with verified isolated faults and independently checked controls while retaining exactly one independently trained network per category.
idea_diagnosis.motivation: Current diagnostics observe reserved masks but cannot certify source events, corruption decisions, target alignment or the loss actually optimized. Resolving these uncertainties is actionable at 10% progress, while remaining distinct from exported-predictor parity, convergence and held-out recommendation usefulness.
idea_diagnosis.implementation_notes:
This is a proposed integration, not executable replacement training code: the actual sampler, training loop and loss implementation are not supplied. Preserve the existing report's three directions and treat exported-predictor parity as the next independent audit, rather than claiming provenance replay resolves it.

Add an optional provenance transport path to the actual production sampler/collator. Record category, user ID, source-event indices, branch, crop bounds, original selected labels, corruption decisions, supervised output positions, effective loss weights and existing negative-sampling decisions where applicable. Preserve source-event identities through cropping, padding and corruption. Transport records with their corresponding batch through an internal wrapper that the main loop unwraps; the model and diagnostic loader must still receive (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B×L tensors. Do not rely on worker-local dataset attributes becoming visible in the parent or on prefetched production logs identifying consumed batches. Missing provenance transport must return null with a reason; do not fabricate records from corrupted tensors.

In the main training loop, after all stochastic transformations and immediately before the forward call, capture detached CPU clones of the exact tensors and their associated provenance. Record category, epoch, batch index, forward step and optimizer-update outcome, including skipped updates when applicable. Fix a bounded capture schedule before execution, such as the first two consumed batches of the first completed epoch and the first two of the final executed epoch, retaining at most four records/category. If the final epoch is not known beforehand, replace the latest-epoch diagnostic buffer rather than advancing the loader. Label records as bounded subsets of consumed batches; they are not an exhaustive certificate and need not represent the deployed checkpoint's own training step. Capture consumes no RNG draws, creates no extra iterator and changes no generator wiring, worker persistence, ordering or sampling settings. Record capture overhead because execution consumes the shared budget.

Provide a replay iterable over captured tensor clones to DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), with corresponding trace access through an optional explicit side channel. Preserve all existing ModelView interfaces: view.model is the actual nn.Module; item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data remain compatible. Preserve diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Run model-dependent probes in evaluation/inference mode and restore every module's prior mode and main-process Python, NumPy, CPU and CUDA RNG states in finally. Replay must not advance a production loader. Main-process state restoration does not restore worker-local RNG, loader progress or persistent-worker state; exact training restart is outside this audit.

Use an independently implemented reconstruction checker grounded in supplied public training histories, rather than calling the producer's construction helper. Validate trace indices, crop boundaries, padding, catalog IDs and the declared effective corruption policy against exact captured tensors. Cloze labels must equal the original item at their corresponding source event. Surrounding historical context is legitimate for Cloze training; terminal targets require strictly earlier retained context and exclusion of target and later events by event index. Earlier occurrences of the same item remain legitimate. Verify the traced target event is not exposed through shifted supervision elsewhere in bidirectional input. The supplied corrected task uses reserved-mask supervision; record and check that effective policy rather than substituting BERT's generic 80/10/10 convention. Trace assertions establish consistency with recorded public histories, not cryptographic authenticity or complete pipeline correctness.

Trace supervision through the actual loss call. Capture detached logits or the exact scorer outputs already produced by the training forward, labels, selected indices, weights, negative IDs and reduction metadata for the bounded records. Independently recompute the declared loss from those same forward outputs without another stochastic forward pass. This checks loss wiring and reduction, not gradients through the entire network. For a sampled loss, retain its actual proposal, exclusions, accidental-hit handling and negative reduction; do not replace it with full-catalog cross-entropy. Require scalar loss agreement using predeclared tolerances appropriate to the recorded dtype, and report absolute/relative discrepancies and valid counts. Check ignored positions have zero direct contribution to the supervised loss; they may still influence supervised positions through attention or receive gradients from regularization. Record auxiliary and regularization terms separately. If the required outputs or loss specification are unavailable, report the check unavailable rather than inferring correctness from margins. A replay under the final evaluation checkpoint does not reproduce the historical training loss; same-forward capture is required for that assertion.

Calibrate detectors on copied records only; never train or select checkpoints using mutants. Predefine operator applicability. A shifted-label fault must produce a verified changed alignment or loss-relevant target; repeated IDs can make some shifts behaviorally equivalent. A restored-target fault applies only to a genuinely masked supervised target under the effective policy. Record original/changed values, intended violated property and independently verified injection success outside the detector. Include unchanged clean records only after independently checking their validity, plus harmless transformations with explicit preconditions, such as a bijective batch-row permutation applied consistently to tensors and provenance. Restoration checks must reproduce original records exactly. Do not treat detector disagreement or model scores as a correctness oracle.

For each operator, report attempted, inapplicable, invalid, proven-equivalent, unresolved, verified-corruption, detected and surviving counts with reasons. Define detection coverage as detected verified corruptions divided by applicable, valid, verified non-equivalent injected corruptions; return null for zero denominator. Unresolved cases remain separately visible and cannot be silently classified as equivalent. Report false-positive rate on independently verified clean/harmless controls separately, with operator-specific denominators. These are bounded fixture summaries, not estimates of real-world fault prevalence. Do not tune assertions to the same calibration cases without logging that adaptation; reserve predefined edge-case fixtures for a final detector check where feasible. Cover empty, short, full-length, unequal-left-padding and repeated-item cases, and report unsupported cases.

Return metrics, metric_definitions, assertion-specific denominators, failures, unavailable reasons, capture schedule and provenance artifacts beneath the current trial directory. Include measured evidence and definitions in the interpretation prompt, distinguishing consumed-batch evidence, synthetic controls, training-exposed recovery, deployment parity and host validation. Repeated item-ID equality alone must never be presented as proof of leakage. Preserve existing family-safe margin and embedding diagnostics, marking item categories, review content, ratings, commercial attributes and simulator traits unavailable. Qualitative feedback can motivate later hypotheses but cannot supply observed compatibility, ownership or demand labels.

Keep left padding, greatest-nonpadding-position readout, reserved-mask appended inference, all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the twenty designated real training users, five/category. No model architecture or scoring change is required; checkpoint configuration and embedded predictor writer must remain consistent. Fresh-process predictor parity remains unavailable unless a supported reload runner actually exercises the deployed writer, item mapping, routing and checkpoint. Deploy one selected checkpoint/category without averaging, additional fitted scorers or score fusion. Do not read other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

All host execution, diagnostics, debugging and failures consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Only pinned host four-category macro validation HR@10 selects model revisions; audit scores do not replace it. Bound and log adaptive diagnostic/validation queries. Report optimization effort separately: integrity does not establish convergence, and convergence or validation accuracy does not establish supervision integrity. The audit introduces no learned shortcut itself, but existing popularity or exposure shortcuts can remain even if every assertion passes. No held-out gain is claimed.

for category in fixed_four_categories:

class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        state = capture_module_modes_and_main_process_rng()
        try:
            view.model.eval()
            with inference_mode():
                # train_loader here replays captured tensors; no production iteration.
                metrics, definitions = existing_family_safe_diagnostics(train_loader)
                records = explicit_optional_consumed_record_side_channel()
                if records is unavailable:
                    record_null_with_reason('sampler_provenance')
                else:
                    for record in records:
                        expected = independently_reconstruct_from_public_histories(record.trace)
                        check_indices_crops_padding_ids_and_exact_tensors(expected, record)
                        check_same_event_cloze_labels_and_effective_corruption_policy(record)
                        if record.trace.branch == 'terminal':
                            check_context_event_indices_strictly_precede_target(record)
                        check_no_shifted_target_event_exposure(record)
                        if exact_same_forward_loss_inputs_are_available(record):
                            expected_loss = independently_recompute_declared_loss(record)
                            check_loss_agreement_with_declared_dtype_tolerances(expected_loss, record)
                            check_ignored_positions_have_zero_direct_supervised_loss(record)
                        else:
                            record_null_with_reason('actual_loss_wiring')
                        accumulate_assertion_counts_failures_and_availability()
                    for record in predefined_calibration_subset(records):
                        clean_status = independently_verify_control(record)
                        record_clean_control_results_only_when_valid(clean_status)
                        for operator in ['shift_label_index', 'restore_masked_target']:
                            applicability = verify_operator_preconditions(record, operator)
                            if not applicability:
                                record_inapplicable_case(operator)
                                continue
                            mutant, injection_evidence = mutate_copy(record, operator)
                            status = independently_verify_changed_property_and_validity(
                                record, mutant, injection_evidence)
                            classify_invalid_equivalent_unresolved_or_verified_corruption(status)
                            if status == 'verified_non_equivalent_corruption':
                                record_detector_result_by_assertion(mutant, operator)
                        test_predeclared_verified_harmless_controls(record)
                    summarize_verified_corruption_detection_and_clean_false_positive_rates()
                return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
        finally:
            restore_module_modes_and_main_process_rng(state)

# Exact loader restart and worker-state restoration are not claimed.
# Check deployed predictor separately only when a supported reload runner exists.

        require=['fault_applicability', 'verified_injections', 'excluded_case_counts',
                 'clean_control_false_positives', 'unavailable_reasons'],
        prohibit=['invented_validation_gains', 'causal_preference_claims',
                  'equivalence_from_survival', 'ensemble_proposals'],
        require_single_model_BERT4Rec_revisions=True)

originality.negative: Tracing, independent replay, loss checks and mutation testing are established techniques; the contribution is a careful task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides actionable evidence for controlled sampler and loss experiments while separating production integrity, deployment consistency and ranking quality.
future_potential.negative: Finite captures cannot certify all execution paths, and passing integrity checks neither improves ranking directly nor resolves the qualitative usefulness failures.

evolution_history.description: Increase terminal-mask supervision within the corrected BERT4Rec, testing endpoint recency separately from training-negative count and loss changes. Train exactly one independent model per category, preserving the bidirectional masked-item backbone and appended-mask inference.
evolution_history.motivation: The proposal explicitly targets two reported user failures: historical interests outweighing present priorities, and broadly plausible recommendations displacing stronger specific next choices. Recent endpoints emphasize more current observations, while terminal supervision removes future context and trains the actual next-choice task. These mechanisms provide hypotheses rather than evidence of improved compatibility, ownership awareness, duplication avoidance, or mood inference. Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile margins and wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%, motivating evaluation of lower-tail discrimination. Near-zero mean item-embedding cosine similarity provides no reason to prioritize an anti-collapse intervention.
evolution_history.implementation_notes:
Modify the host-supplied corrected baseline rather than reconstructing its unavailable implementation. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution per trial. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory and never read other trials or checkpoints. Preserve the host optimizer, updates and baseline objective for the initial masking/endpoint comparison. Do not silently replace a different baseline loss with pairwise logistic loss; declare that replacement as a separate experimental factor.

Define a training history H=(x_1,...,x_n), with n>=2. Uniformly sample eligible users, then sample endpoint t in {2,...,n} before truncation. The uniform condition uses P(t)=1/(n-1); the exponential condition uses P(t) proportional to 2^(-(n-t)/10), equivalently alpha=2^(-1/10), approximately 0.9330. The ten-interaction half-life is a proposed setting, not a validated result. Retain the earlier 50% uniform/50% exponential endpoint mixture as an optional, separately declared follow-up rather than conflating it with the primary exponential condition. Sample the terminal branch independently with q=0.5; reconstruction-only uses q=0.

For terminal examples, input is left_pad(last_{L-1}(x_1,...,x_{t-1})+[MASK], L), label x_t. Exclude the target occurrence and entire suffix; legitimate earlier repetitions may remain. In zero-based code, use H[:t] and target H[t] with t sampled from {1,...,n-1}. For reconstruction examples, use the training-only prefix H[:t+1] under that indexing, retain its last L items, select each nonpadding position independently with probability 0.15, and force one uniformly selected nonpadding target if none is selected. Replace every selected occurrence with the reserved MASK token; do not leave selected targets unchanged. Reconstruction permits bidirectional context within this prefix, as BERT4Rec intends. Define candidate CE explicitly for positive logit p and sampled negative logits n_j: L_CE = log(1 + sum_j exp(n_j-p)), implemented with stable cross-entropy or logsumexp. Use no logQ adjustment. CE has one loss per valid target; apply that same across-target/example weighting, while acknowledging that objective geometry and gradient magnitudes remain different. A repeated negative appearing m times contributes m*exp(n) to CE's denominator, equivalent to n+log(m), and m repeated terms to summed BCE. """Per-dataset BERT4Rec baseline for Amazon Reviews.

Trains one independent BERT4Rec checkpoint per dataset while sharing one default
hyper-parameter profile across datasets. The generated predict.py routes by the
optional dataset_name keyword used by the RecHarness Amazon Reviews harness.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import os
import pickle
import random
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

DEFAULT_DATASETS = [
    "Movies_and_TV",
    "Industrial_and_Scientific",
    "Electronics",
    "CDs_and_Vinyl",
]
DATASETS = [
    part.strip()
    for part in os.environ.get("GAGC_DATASETS", ",".join(DEFAULT_DATASETS)).split(",")
    if part.strip()
]

def _read_split(path: str) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
    data: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return {}
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.strip().split()
            if len(parts) == 2:
                data[int(parts[0])].append(int(parts[1]))
    return dict(data)


def _load_itemnum(data_dir: str, dataset_name: str) -> int:
    stats_path = os.path.join(data_dir, "dataset_stats.json")
    if os.path.isfile(stats_path):
        with open(stats_path) as f:
            stats = json.load(f)
        if dataset_name in stats:
            return int(stats[dataset_name]["itemnum"])
    itemnum = 0
    for split in ("train", "valid"):
        path = os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_{split}.txt")
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                parts = line.strip().split()
                if len(parts) == 2:
                    itemnum = max(itemnum, int(parts[1]))
    return itemnum


def load_dataset(dataset_name: str, data_dir: str):
    user_train = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_train.txt"))
    user_valid = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_valid.txt"))
    itemnum = _load_itemnum(data_dir, dataset_name)
    return user_train, user_valid, itemnum


### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Count-matched candidate CE and BPR with unchanged corruption
# The supplied objective is single-negative BPR, not BCE.
# Separate runs: bpr/K=1, bpr/K=16, ce/K=16. Never combine checkpoints.
# K=1 CE equals BPR, so that configuration need not be trained twice.
# The unchanged host baseline remains the external benchmark anchor;
# purpose-separated sampling below defines the matched experimental controls.
# Preserve terminal allocation, endpoint distribution and reconstruction policy.
TERMINAL_MASK_PROBABILITY = 0.5
ENDPOINT_HALF_LIFE = 10.0
RECONSTRUCTION_MASK_PROBABILITY = 0.15
TRAIN_OBJECTIVE = os.environ.get("BERT4REC_OBJECTIVE", "ce").lower()
TRAIN_NEGATIVES = int(os.environ.get("BERT4REC_NEGATIVES", "16"))
if TRAIN_OBJECTIVE not in {"bpr", "ce"}:
    raise ValueError("BERT4REC_OBJECTIVE must be bpr or ce")
if TRAIN_NEGATIVES not in {1, 16}:
    raise ValueError("BERT4REC_NEGATIVES must be 1 or 16")


def sample_batch(
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]],
    itemnum: int,
    batch_size: int,
    maxlen: int,
    num_negatives: int = 1,
    rngs=None,
):
    # Default output remains three B x L arrays for diagnostic adapters.
    # Only the explicit training caller requests B x L x K negatives.
    if maxlen < 2 or batch_size < 1 or num_negatives < 1:
        raise ValueError("require maxlen >= 2, positive batch_size and negatives")
    window_rng, corruption_rng, negative_rng = (
        rngs if rngs is not None else (random, random, random)
    )
    users = [u for u, items in user_train.items() if len(items) >= 2]
    if not users:
        raise RuntimeError("no users with at least two training interactions")
    batch_seq, batch_pos, batch_neg = [], [], []
    for _ in range(batch_size):
        history = user_train[window_rng.choice(users)]
        # Preserve the supplied zero-based endpoint distribution.
        # P(t) is proportional to 2 ** (-(n - 1 - t) / 10).
        endpoint = window_rng.choices(
            range(1, len(history)),
            weights=[
                2.0 ** (-(len(history) - 1 - t) / ENDPOINT_HALF_LIFE)
                for t in range(1, len(history))
            ],
            k=1,
        )[0]
        terminal = corruption_rng.random() < TERMINAL_MASK_PROBABILITY
        items = history[max(0, endpoint + 1 - maxlen) : endpoint + 1]
        seq = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        pos = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        neg = np.zeros((maxlen, num_negatives), dtype=np.int64)
        seq[-len(items) :] = items
        eligible = list(range(maxlen - len(items), maxlen))
        if terminal:
            # Only the endpoint is supervised; its occurrence is replaced below.
            # No suffix or shifted target is exposed to the bidirectional encoder.
            selected = [maxlen - 1]
        else:
            selected = [
                i
                for i in eligible
                if corruption_rng.random() < RECONSTRUCTION_MASK_PROBABILITY
            ]
            if not selected:
                selected = [corruption_rng.choice(eligible)]
        interacted = set(history)
        if len(interacted) >= itemnum:
            raise RuntimeError("no unobserved negative item available")
        for i in selected:
            pos[i] = seq[i]
            seq[i] = itemnum + 1
            # Exactly one stream draw per target makes later target seeds
            # independent of K and of rejection counts. Each target then uses
            # independent uniform rejection draws WITH replacement, excluding
            # the same full training history as the supplied sampler.
            target_rng = random.Random(negative_rng.getrandbits(64))
            for j in range(num_negatives):
                item = target_rng.randint(1, itemnum)
                while item in interacted:
                    item = target_rng.randint(1, itemnum)
                neg[i, j] = item
        batch_seq.append(seq)
        batch_pos.append(pos)
        batch_neg.append(neg[:, 0] if num_negatives == 1 else neg)
    return np.asarray(batch_seq), np.asarray(batch_pos), np.asarray(batch_neg)


### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END


def _history_to_tensor(
    history: list[int], maxlen: int, device: torch.device
) -> torch.Tensor:
    seq_arr = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    for i, item in enumerate(reversed(history[-maxlen:])):
        seq_arr[maxlen - 1 - i] = item
    return torch.tensor([seq_arr], dtype=torch.long, device=device)


def evaluate_val(
    model: nn.Module,
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]],
    user_valid: dict[int, list[int]],
    itemnum: int,
    device: torch.device,
    maxlen: int,
    num_users: int = 200,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Reproducible validation without consuming training randomness
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    val_users = [u for u in user_valid if u in user_train and user_valid[u]]
    if len(val_users) > num_users:
        val_users = rng.sample(val_users, num_users)
    ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
    if not val_users:
        return {"HR@10": 0.0, "HR@20": 0.0, "NDCG@10": 0.0, "NDCG@20": 0.0}

    hr10 = hr20 = ndcg10 = ndcg20 = 0.0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for user in val_users:
            target = user_valid[user][0]
            history = user_train[user]
            interacted = set(history) | {target, 0}
            ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Fixed unique validation negatives with bounded sampling
            available_count = itemnum - sum(1 <= item <= itemnum for item in interacted)
            if available_count < 99:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"validation user {user} has only {available_count} eligible negatives; "
                    "99 unique negatives are required"
                )
            candidates = [target]
            if available_count < 198:
                available = [
                    item for item in range(1, itemnum + 1) if item not in interacted
                ]
                candidates.extend(rng.sample(available, 99))
            else:
                while len(candidates) < 100:
                    neg_item = rng.randint(1, itemnum)
                    if neg_item not in interacted:
                        interacted.add(neg_item)
                        candidates.append(neg_item)
            ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
            seq_t = _history_to_tensor(history, maxlen, device)
            cand_t = torch.tensor(candidates, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            scores = model.score_candidates(seq_t, cand_t).detach().cpu().tolist()
            rank = sorted(range(len(scores)), key=lambda i: -scores[i]).index(0)
            hr10 += 1.0 if rank < 10 else 0.0
            hr20 += 1.0 if rank < 20 else 0.0
            ndcg10 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 10 else 0.0
            ndcg20 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 20 else 0.0

        "HR@20": hr20 / n,
        "NDCG@10": ndcg10 / n,

    model: nn.Module, seq: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, neg: torch.Tensor

            d_model=hidden_units,
            nhead=num_heads,
            dim_feedforward=hidden_units * 4,

            batch_first=True,
            norm_first=True,

        pos = pos * (seq != 0).long()

            sequence, dtype=torch.long, device=self.item_emb.weight.device
        )
        return self.encode_sequence(sequence)

    def predict_score(
        self, features: torch.Tensor, items: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:

            items, dtype=torch.long, device=self.item_emb.weight.device
        )
        embeddings = self.item_emb(items)
        if items.shape == features.shape[:-1]:
            return (features * embeddings).sum(dim=-1)
        if items.ndim == 1:
            return torch.matmul(features, embeddings.transpose(0, 1))
        if items.ndim == features.ndim and items.shape[:-1] == features.shape[:-1]:
            return torch.matmul(embeddings, features.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)

            f"Unsupported feature/item shapes: {tuple(features.shape)}, {tuple(items.shape)}"

        self, seq: torch.Tensor, candidates: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:

            raise ValueError("Candidates must have shape K or B x K")
        if candidates.ndim == 2 and candidates.shape[0] != seq.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError("Per-user candidates must match the history batch size")

        # Retain the final L-1 history slots and append the reserved MASK.
        # Left padding remains left padding, including for empty histories.
        prediction_seq = torch.zeros_like(seq)
        prediction_seq[:, :-1] = seq[:, 1:]
        prediction_seq[:, -1] = self.mask_token
        features = self.log2feats(prediction_seq)[:, -1, :]
        # The appended MASK is the final nonpadding position, even when the
        # history is short. Never use nonpadding-count minus one here.
        embeddings = self.item_emb(candidates)
        if candidates.ndim == 1:
            scores = torch.matmul(features, embeddings.transpose(0, 1))
        else:
            scores = torch.bmm(embeddings, features.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
        return scores[0] if seq.shape[0] == 1 else scores

        return result

    @staticmethod
    def _summary(values):
        values = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
        if values.size == 0:
            return {
                "mean": None,
                "count": 0,
                "ci95": None,
                "reason": "No eligible user observations",
            }
        if not np.isfinite(values).all():
            raise ValueError("Nonfinite observations in diagnostic bootstrap")
        rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
        indices = rng.integers(0, values.size, size=(1000, values.size))
        means = values[indices].mean(axis=1)
        return {
            "mean": float(values.mean()),
            "count": int(values.size),
            "ci95": np.quantile(means, [0.025, 0.975]).tolist(),
            "reason": None,
        }

    def _history_sensitivity(self):
        histories = self.user_train.get("History", self.user_train)
        itemnum = int(self.network.itemnum)
        length = int(self.network.maxlen)
        eligible = []
        popularity = Counter()
        for user, events in histories.items():
            events = list(events)
            if any(int(x) < 1 or int(x) > itemnum for x in events):
                raise ValueError("Training history contains a noncatalog item ID")
            events = [int(x) for x in events]
            popularity.update(events)
            # One last training event per user; all later events are absent.
            prefix = events[:-1][-(length - 1) :] if length > 1 else []
            if len(prefix) >= 2:
                eligible.append((user, events, prefix, events[-1]))
        eligible.sort(key=lambda row: str(row[0]))
        if len(eligible) > 200:
            eligible = random.Random(42).sample(eligible, 200)
        length_cuts = (
            np.quantile([len(row[2]) for row in eligible], [0.25, 0.5, 0.75]).tolist()
            if eligible
            else []
        )
        pop_cuts = (
            np.quantile(
                [popularity[i] for i in range(1, itemnum + 1)], [0.25, 0.5, 0.75]
            ).tolist()
            if itemnum
            else []
        )
        rows = {seed: [] for seed in (42, 43, 44)}
        names = [
            "original",
            "compact_oldest",
            "compact_newest",
            "mask_oldest",
            "mask_newest",
        ]
        for user, events, prefix, target in eligible:
            k = min(3, len(prefix) // 2)
            base = self._pack_inference(prefix)
            old_mask, new_mask = base.copy(), base.copy()
            first = length - 1 - len(prefix)
            old_mask[first : first + k] = [self.network.mask_token] * k
            new_mask[length - 1 - k : length - 1] = [self.network.mask_token] * k
            inputs = [
                base,
                self._pack_inference(prefix[k:]),
                self._pack_inference(prefix[:-k]),
                old_mask,
                new_mask,
            ]
            seq = torch.tensor(inputs, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
            features = self.network.encode_sequence(seq)[:, -1]
            excluded = set(events) | {0, target, int(self.network.mask_token)}
            available_count = itemnum - sum(1 <= x <= itemnum for x in excluded)
            for seed in (42, 43, 44):
                # Stable user-specific RNG; candidate sets are frozen for all interventions.
                rng = random.Random(f"{seed}:{user}")
                count = min(99, available_count)
                if available_count < 198:
                    pool = [x for x in range(1, itemnum + 1) if x not in excluded]
                    negatives = rng.sample(pool, count)
                else:
                    negatives, used = [], set()
                    while len(negatives) < count:
                        candidate = rng.randint(1, itemnum)
                        if candidate not in excluded and candidate not in used:
                            used.add(candidate)
                            negatives.append(candidate)
                candidates = torch.tensor([target] + negatives, device=self.device)
                scores = (
                    (features @ self.network.item_emb(candidates).T)
                    .float()
                    .cpu()
                    .numpy()
                )
                if not np.isfinite(scores).all():
                    raise ValueError("Nonfinite diagnostic candidate scores")
                measured, tops = {}, {}
                for index, name in enumerate(names):
                    order = np.argsort(-scores[index], kind="stable")
                    rank = int(np.flatnonzero(order == 0)[0]) + 1
                    tops[name] = set(order[:10].tolist())
                    measured[name] = {
                        "target_score": float(scores[index, 0]),
                        "rank": rank,
                        "hr10": float(rank <= 10),
                        "margin": (
                            float(scores[index, 0] - scores[index, 1:].max())
                            if count
                            else None
                        ),
                    }
                for name in names[1:]:
                    measured[name]["top10_overlap"] = len(
                        tops[name] & tops["original"]
                    ) / min(len(tops[name]), len(tops["original"]))
                    for metric in ("target_score", "rank", "hr10", "margin"):
                        value = measured[name][metric]
                        measured[name]["delta_" + metric] = (
                            value - measured["original"][metric]
                            if value is not None
                            else None
                        )
                for mode in ("compact", "mask"):
                    measured[mode + "_recent_minus_older"] = {
                        metric: (
                            (
                                measured[mode + "_newest"][metric]
                                - measured[mode + "_oldest"][metric]
                            )
                            if measured[mode + "_newest"][metric] is not None
                            else None
                        )
                        for metric in (
                            "target_score",
                            "rank",
                            "hr10",
                            "margin",
                            "top10_overlap",
                        )
                    }
                rows[seed].append(
                    {
                        "user": str(user),
                        "repeat": target in prefix,
                        "length_quartile": int(
                            np.searchsorted(length_cuts, len(prefix), side="right")
                        ),
                        "popularity_quartile": int(
                            np.searchsorted(pop_cuts, popularity[target], side="right")
                        ),
                        "candidate_count": count + 1,
                        "measurements": measured,
                    }
                )

        # Keep metric keys and explicit null summaries in empty strata.
        metric_keys = {
            name + "." + metric
            for records in rows.values()
            for record in records
            for name, measurements in record["measurements"].items()
            for metric in measurements
        }
        if not metric_keys:
            for name in names:
                metrics = ["target_score", "rank", "hr10", "margin"]
                if name != "original":
                    metrics += [
                        "top10_overlap",
                        "delta_target_score",
                        "delta_rank",
                        "delta_hr10",
                        "delta_margin",
                    ]
                metric_keys.update(name + "." + metric for metric in metrics)
            for mode in ("compact", "mask"):
                metric_keys.update(
                    mode + "_recent_minus_older." + metric
                    for metric in (
                        "target_score",
                        "rank",
                        "hr10",
                        "margin",
                        "top10_overlap",
                    )
                )

        def aggregate(records):
            output = {key: [] for key in sorted(metric_keys)}
            for record in records:
                for name, measurements in record["measurements"].items():
                    for metric, value in measurements.items():
                        if value is not None:
                            output[name + "." + metric].append(value)
            return {key: self._summary(values) for key, values in output.items()}

        draws = {}
        for seed, records in rows.items():
            draws[str(seed)] = {
                "users": len(records),
                "candidate_counts": dict(
                    Counter(r["candidate_count"] for r in records)
                ),
                "summary": aggregate(records),
                "repeat_explore": {
                    label: {
                        "users": sum(r["repeat"] == repeat for r in records),
                        "summary": aggregate(
                            [r for r in records if r["repeat"] == repeat]
                        ),
                    }
                    for label, repeat in (("repeat", True), ("explore", False))
                },
                "strata": {
                    field: {
                        str(q): {
                            "users": sum(r[field] == q for r in records),
                            "summary": aggregate([r for r in records if r[field] == q]),
                        }
                        for q in range(4)
                    }
                    for field in ("length_quartile", "popularity_quartile")
                },
            }
        return {
            "exposure": "training-exposed recovery; not held-out generalization",
            "category": getattr(self.view, "dataset_name", None),
            "eligible_selected_users": len(eligible),
            "reason": (
                None
                if eligible
                else "No training prefix with at least two retained items"
            ),
            "selection_seed": 42,
            "bootstrap_seed": 42,
            "bootstrap_resamples": 1000,
            "length_quartile_cutpoints": length_cuts,
            "item_training_popularity_quartile_cutpoints": pop_cuts,
            "candidate_policy": (
                "Positive exactly once; up to 99 unique catalog negatives excluding all "
                "permitted training-history items, positive, padding and mask. Frozen across interventions."
            ),
            "draws": draws,
            "category_metadata_breakdowns": {},
            "equal_category_macro": None,
            "equal_category_macro_reason": "A single ModelView cannot certify eligibility of all four categories",
        }
